"N.-C. D. N." SPECIAL SERVICE
Washington, Mar. 10.
The complaint* in the divorce
action brought on behalf of Mr. L.
Hoover, described as an American
aviator now living in China, against
Muriel de Vere Littleton Hoover
was published in this morning's
newspapers.
It describes how Mrs. Hoover met
General George A. L. Dumont, now
French military attaché in Washing-
ton, while she was in China in 1925
and 1926 and asserts an infatuation
started which has continued since
that time.
General Dumont is named as co-
respondent in the action, which, the
newspapers assert, will not be con-
tested by Mrs. Hoover who is
described as an "English beauty."
The suit has aroused considerable
local interest as General Dumont is
widely known in social circles here.

《字林西报》，1929年3月12日，星期二。

L. 胡佛离婚案

续：妻子据称迷恋在中国结识的一名男子

“字林西报”特约服务
华盛顿，3月10日电。
代表现居中国的美国飞行员 L. 胡佛先生，针对穆里尔·德·维尔·利特尔顿·胡佛（Muriel de Vere Littleton Hoover）提起的离婚诉讼中的诉状*，刊登在今晨的报纸上。
诉状描述了胡佛太太于1925年和1926年在中国期间，结识了现任驻华盛顿法国武官乔治·A·L·杜蒙将军（General George A. L. Dumont），并声称由此产生了一种痴迷，且一直持续至今。
杜蒙将军在该案中被列为共同被告，报纸称，被描述为“英国美女”的胡佛太太将不对此进行抗辩。
由于杜蒙将军在此地的社交圈中广为人知，该诉讼引起了当地相当大的关注。
——合众社。

II a. c. (Pal)
H.R. 1929年3月12日

Lawerence E. de S. Hoover.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C.I.D. REGISTRY
No I. O. 8259
29 June 1926）

Lawerence E. de S. Hoover arrived in Shanghai about June 1925 as an accredited representative of the Auto-Ordnance Corporation of New York. His chief interest in China seems to have been the sale of the Thompson Auto-Rifle and the Thompson Sub-Machine Gun of which latter weapon the Municipal Council in September 1925 purchased from him 16 for the use of the Police. In 1926 he visited Manila, Tientsin, Peking, Mukden and Japan and it is suspected that these visits were in connection with the sale of the guns which he represented, although so far as is known the only business he has put through is the sale of the 16 Thompson Sub-Machine Guns to the Municipal Police. He has also paid one or two visits to the Chinese officials in Chapei, his excuse being that he wanted to find out whether any guns were leaking into Chapei. These visits have caused suspicion, but there is nothing definite to go on.

In May 1926, Hoover approached the Manager of the Operating Department of the Standard Oil Coy., re the sale of Thompson Sub-Machine Guns for the Company's up river steam boats. At the time Hoover stated it was necessary for the Company to make application for a "Huchow" through their Consul before they would be allowed to import such guns into China. This was done, but the American Minister could not see his way to make application for this special permit to the Chinese Government to import such class of guns as it was not consistent with the "Importation of Arms for Foreigners Arms Regulations promulgated at Peking in 1908".

Hoover's conduct here seems to have incurred the displeasure of his employers who repeatedly cabled him to return to New York and on the expiry of his contract in May 1926 dispensed with his services. It is also said that he has a private income which made him independent of the position he held with the Auto-Ordnance Corporation. It would appear, however, that this source of financial revenue is almost exhausted as he was posted at the American Club for non-payment and struck off the list of membership about two months ago.

Hoover's knowledge of the mechanism and parts of the Thompson Sub-Machine Gun and other similar weapons is recognised to be that of an expert.

With reference to the suspicion resting on Hoover re his connection with gun running and arms smugglers, it is known that he is friendly with Hoffman, who is suspected arms dealer and who lives in the Astor House, and with the notorious arms smugglers Elly Widler, yet it is significant that his name has not been mentioned in reference to any arms transactions reported, although at the recent trial of Worthington and Chalet at the American Court he was a frequent and interested visitor.

The information that he intends to visit Afghanistan has been frequently uttered by Hoover, who has stated his intention to enter India at Karachi and proceed via Afghanistan, Ispahan, the Persian Gulf of Aden to Africa. This journey to anyone who knows the country would be fraught with danger and is considered more a boast on Hoover's part than a reality.

Hoover has also been seen in the American Club wearing a Police armlet and lanyard with pistol although he never was a member of the Police Specials or the S.V.C. He is at present residing at 331 Route Cardinal Mercier. He is being carefully shadowed.

Jle Res

劳伦斯 E. de S. 胡佛。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事调查处档案室
编号 I. O. 8259
1926年6月29日）

劳伦斯 E. de S. 胡佛于1925年6月左右抵达上海，身份是纽约自动军械公司（Auto-Ordnance Corporation）的认证代表。他在中国的主要兴趣似乎是销售汤普森自动步枪和汤普森冲锋枪，后一种武器工部局于1925年9月从他手中购买了16支供警察使用。1926年，他访问了马尼拉、天津、北京、沈阳和日本，有人怀疑这些访问与他所代表的枪支销售有关，尽管据所知，他完成的唯一业务就是向市政警察出售了16支汤普森冲锋枪。他还曾一两次拜访闸北的中国官员，借口是他想查明是否有枪支流入闸北。这些访问引起了怀疑，但没有确切的依据。

1926年5月，胡佛接洽美孚石油公司（Standard Oil Coy.）运营部经理，商讨为公司内河轮船销售汤普森冲锋枪事宜。当时胡佛表示，公司必须通过其领事申请“护照”（Huchow），才能获准将此类枪支进口到中国。虽然这样做了，但美国公使认为无法向中国政府申请此类枪支进口的特别许可，因为这不符合“1908年在北京颁布的《外国人枪械进口章程》”。

胡佛在此地的行为似乎惹恼了他的雇主，他们多次发电报让他返回纽约，并在1926年5月合同到期时解除了他的职务。另有说法称，他有私人收入，使其不依赖于在自动军械公司担任的职位。然而，这一财源似乎已几乎耗尽，因为他因未付款而被美国总会点名，并在大约两个月前被除名。

胡佛对汤普森冲锋枪及其他类似武器的机械结构和部件的了解，被公认为具有专家水平。

关于对胡佛与枪支走私者和军火走私犯有联系的怀疑，已知他与住在礼查饭店（Astor House）、涉嫌为军火商的霍夫曼（Hoffman）以及臭名昭著的军火走私犯埃利·维德勒（Elly Widler）关系友好，但值得注意的是，在任何已报告的军火交易中均未提及他的名字，尽管在最近沃辛顿（Worthington）和夏莱（Chalet）在美国法院受审期间，他是一名频繁且感兴趣的旁听者。

胡佛经常声称他打算访问阿富汗，他表示打算在卡拉奇进入印度，然后经由阿富汗、伊斯法罕、波斯湾和亚丁湾前往非洲。对于了解该国情况的人来说，这次旅程充满危险，被认为更多是胡佛的吹嘘而非现实。

还有人看到胡佛在美国总会佩戴警用臂章和挂绳，并携带手枪，尽管他从未成为警察后备队（Police Specials）或上海万国商团（S.V.C.）的成员。他目前居住在梅爱禄路（Route Cardinal Mercier）331号。他正受到严密监视。

Jle Res
2月6日

                  CENTRAL I. O.
                  August      9,      1927

REPORT ON Lawrence E. de S. Hoover.

Made by D.S.I. Robertson.   Forwarded by J McGivens A.C.P.

Sir,
        Lawrence E. de S. Hoover arrived in Shanghai
about June 1925 as an accredited representative of the Auto-
Ordnance Corporation of New York. His chief interest in China
seems to have been the sale of the Thompson Auto-Rifle and
and the Thompson Sub-Machine Gun of which latter weapon the
Municipal Council in September 1925 purchased from him 16 for
the use of the Police. In 1926 he visited Manila, Tientsin,
Peking, Mukden and Japan and it is suspected that these visits
were in connection with the sale of the guns which he represented,
although so far as is known the only business he has put through
is the sale of the 16 Thompson Sub-Machine Guns to the Municipal
Police. He has also paid one or two visits to Chinese
officials in Chapei, his excuse being that he wanted to find
out whether any guns were leaking into Chapei. These visits
have caused suspicion, but there is nothing definite to go on.
        In May 1926 Hoover approached the Manager of the
Operating Department of the Standard Oil Coy., re the sale of
Thompson Sub Machine Guns for the Company's up river steamers
boats. At the time Hoover stated it was necessary for the
Company to make application for a "Huchow" through their
Consul before they would be allowed to import such guns into
China. This was done, but the American Minister could not see
his way to make application for this special permit to the
Chinese Government to import such class of guns as it was not
consistent with the "Importation of Arms for Foreigners Arms
Regulations promulgated at Peking in 1908".

Hoover's conduct here seems to have incurred the
displeasure of his employers who repeatedly cabled him to
return to New York and on the expiry of his contract in May
1926 dispensed with his services. It is also said that he has
a private income which made him independent of the position
he held with the Auto-Ordnance Corporation. It would appear,
however, that this source of financial revenue is almost
exhausted as he was posted at the American Club for non-payment
and struck off the list of membership about two months ago.
Hoover's knowledge of the mechanism and parts of the
Thompson Sub-Machine Gun and other similar weapons is
recognized to be that of an expert.
With reference to the suspicion resting on Hoover
re his connections with gun running and arms smugglers, it is
known that he is friendly with Hoffman, who is a suspected
arms dealer and who lives in the Astor House, and with the
notorious arms smuggler Elly Widler, yet it is significant
that his name has not been mentioned in reference to any
arms transactions reported, although at the recent trial of
Worthington and Chalet at the American Court he was a
frequent and interested visitor.
The information that he intends to visit Afghanistan
has been frequently uttered by Hoover, who has stated his
intention to enter India at Karachi and proceed via Afghanistan,
Ispahan, the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Aden to Africa. This
journey to anyone who knows the country would be fraught with
